content.text: {"subject":"Photosynthesis and Chlorophyll","story":"Ishika notices her houseplant looks droopy near the window, so she moves it to sunlight and waters it. Within days, it's green and perky again. Her science teacher explains: leaves are green because they contain chlorophyll, a pigment that captures sunlight and converts it into food for the plant. Green light bounces off leaves (that's why we see green), while blue and red light are absorbed to power photosynthesis. Without sunlight, plants can't make this food, so they weaken. Now Ishika understands—the green color isn't just pretty; it's proof the plant is working hard, turning sun into strength.","abhyasaApplicable":true,"abhyasaPrompt":"Next time you see a plant looking pale or yellow instead of green, what do you think might be missing—and how would you help it?"}
